new_statements.relation_note: Stress not phonemic; no tone; no length contrast.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is reported as non-phonemic (not contrastive); no position for word stress is given. The language has no tone and no contrastive vowel length. Syllable patterns V, CV, CVC, VC; five vowels /i e a o u/ plus diphthongs ei eu oe oi ou (and ae ai au written as sequences).
new_statements.identity_note: Header reads 'Bemal (Kein) Language [BMH] - Madang Province'; SIL record subject language Kein [bmh]; villages listed (Bemal, Jobto, Jall, Baisarik, Sekuar) match Z'graggen 1975 PL B-41's C4 Bemal (Kein) villages (Bemal, Jal, Jobto, Sakwari, Wehege). This is the SIL-PNG OPD the the compilation wished for ('existence unconfirmed'). P. Lillie was the SIL Girawa (sister language) worker.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang district, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University.
sources.note: p. 13: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet' — a blanket remark about the survey's broad phonetic transcription, not about Kein, which is not among the languages covered (Kein/Bemal was first recorded in Z'graggen's 1971-72 fieldwork).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid kein1239 and reference tables for kein1239, koko1271 (Kokon) and mabu1247 (Mabuso)
sources.note: Only two references for Kein (Z'graggen 1975, 1980), none descriptive. Kokon-subgroup references (64) are all Girawa (Lillie, Gassmann; Gasaway & Sims 1992 'Girawa grammar') or Munit ('Berin phonology', Elliott & Elliott 1977); Mabuso references (148) add Amele, Bau, Nobonob, Wagi items — no Kein-specific description anywhere.

sources.citation: Gasaway, Eileen & Heather Sims. 1992. Girawa grammar. Ukarumpa: SIL. 145 pp.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.note: This work describes Girawa (gira1247) [bbr], Kokon family, Mabuso stock, Madang Province, PNG. The work describes Girawa, not Kein/Bemal; the words 'Kein' and 'Bemal' occur on 0 scanned pages of the 145. Nothing here bears on the Kein catalog entry (classification undetermined, cite Lillie 2011 Bemal OPD). Girawa is Kein's closest relative (Kokon subgroup); its phonology chapter would give the nearest-related stress statement, though not a Kein statement

sources.note: Nothing. Fields: Alternate Names Bemal; Population 1,750 (2000 census); Location Madang Province, Trans-Gogol district; Status 5 (Developing); Classification Trans-New Guinea, Madang, Croisilles, Kokon; Dialects Kibam, Sigau, Sog; Typology SOV; Language Use (Tok Pisin first for most children); Language Development 'Taught in primary schools. sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, Australian National University.
sources.note: Nothing on Kein. Documents that the SIL Begesin-area team produced phonology manuscripts only for the sister language Girawa [gira1247]: Gasaway & Sims 1977 'A preliminary phonology of Girawa' TS 41 pp; Lillie 1984 'Girawa phonemes' MS 10 pp; Lillie 1985 'Girawa phonology: the question of stress' MS 1 p; Lillie 1987 'Phonology notes' MS 4 pp; Gasaway & Sims 1992 'Girawa grammar (essentials), revised by Pat Lillie' TS 102+38 pp - nearest-relative stress pointers, another variety.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. xvi+199 pp.
sources.note: Kein appears as 'Bemal' (column C4) in a ~300-item comparative wordlist. Introduction section 6 (pp. viii-ix) says the transcription is 'semi-phonemic' and lists fluctuating consonants per language (Bemal: s~j, z~dz~zy, l~r, d~r); vowel length is written (e.g. 'man' du:) but stress is never marked and the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the volume (checked in both the ANU text and a fresh extracted text run). No statement on Kein stress.
